text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
SIR CHARLES BARRY who designed Britain's House of Parliament was born in 1795.
American actor DOUGLAS FAIRBANKS was born in 1883. He specialized in swashbuckling roles.

US singer ROSEMARY CLOONEY was born in 1928. She was one of the most popular artists in the 1950s. Her first hit was a duet with GUY MITCHELL "You're Just In Love" (1951). She also starred in more than 50 films and after a break in her career re-emerged in the 1970s. Her hits included " Come On-A-My-House" (1951), "Tenderly" (1952), "Hey There" (1954), "This Ole House" (1954), "Mambo Italiano" (1954) and "Mangos" (1957).

British actress JOAN COLLINS was born in 1933. She first gained recognition playing a role in an episode of Star Trek. During the 70s she starred in movies like 'The Bitch' and established a reputation as a screen villain. That reputation saw her gain her greatest fame as the villain in 'Dynasty'.
American musican RICHARD MOOG was born in 1934. He was famous for inventing the Moog synthesizer.
Australian tennis star and Davis Cup Captain JOHN NEWCOMBE was born in 1944.
Australian golfer DAVID GRAHAM was born in 1946.
British guitarist with '10 CC' RICK FENN was born in 1953. He also worked with MIKE OLDFIELD and NICK MASON.
** EVENTS **
1430 : JOAN of Arc was captured at Compiegne and handed
over to the British.
1498 : GIROLAMO SAVONAROLA, Italian religious and
political reformer, was hanged and burnt at the stake.
1533 : Archbishop of Canterbury THOMAS CRAMER declared
Henry VIII's marriage to CATHERINE of Aragon void, and his marriage to ANNE BOLEYN in January legal - infuriating the Vatican.
1618 : The Defenestration of Prague took place, a
Bohemian revolt against the Habsburg Emperor, beginning the Thirty Years War.
1701 : Captain WILLIAM KIDD was hanged for piracy and

murder at London's Execution Dock. KIDD was commissioned by the British government to commit acts of piracy against Spanish and French ships, but soon turned on all merchant ships because of the money he was making.
1785 : BENJAMIN FRANKLIN reveals he had invented bifocal
glasses.
1788 : South Carolina became the eighth state of the
Union.
1868 : KIT CARSON, American frontiersman and soldier who
contributed greatly to the westward expansion of the U.S., died.
1873 : The 'Mounties" were formed in Canada.
1887 : The French crown jewels were sold for six million
francs.
1913 : THOMAS EDISON invented the telephone recorder.
1913 : A speed limit of 10 miles per hour was introduced
at the world's busiest intersection ... at Hyde Park Corner in London.
1915 : Having been neutral, Italy declared war on
Austria-Hungary.
1927 : In Melbourne five men were fined for playing
billiards at Essendon on Anzac Day.
1931 : Overcrowding at football matches was in the
spotlight after several of the 45,000 fans at Melbourne's Richmond ground were injured when a fence gave way.
1934 : American bank robbers BONNIE PARKER and CLYDE
BARROW were shot dead by police. The pair were cut down by more than 50 bullets during an ambush in Louisiana. During their reign of crime they killed 12 people.
1937 : JOHN D. ROCKEFELLER, U.S. multimillionaire and
founder of the Standard Oil Company, died.
1944 : British and U.S. forces launched a massive
offensive from the beach-head at Anzio, Italy.
1945 : HEINRICH HIMMLER, German Nazi leader and Chief of

Police, committed suicide a day after being captured; Admiral KARL DOENITZ and leading members of the German government were arrested; WINSTON CHURCHILL resigned, bringing to an end Britain's wartime coalition.
1949 : The German Federal Republic formally came into
existence with Bonn as the capital, after the signing of the constitution.
1950 : The BBC and sporting representatives agreed to the
televising of 100 sporting events a year.
1950 : In Brisbane the Federal Government announced plans
for a national health scheme based on voluntary insurance.
1960 : Nazi war criminal ADOLF EICHMANN was captured and
taken to Israel to stand trial. EICHMANN was in charge of the Gestapo section which rounded up Jews and sent them to the concentration camps.
1992 : The United States and the Republics of the former
Soviet Union agreed to implement the nuclear arms treaty originally agreed to with the Soviet Union.
1993 : An American man who shot a Japanese exchange

student when he knocked on his door looking for a Halloween party was acquitted by a jury. The jury accepted the man's arguement that he was afraid for his life because of soaring crime rates. The incident caused a major drop in Japanese holiday trips to the US.
1977 : A group of South Moluccan terrorists took over a
school in the Netherlands as part of their push for independence. They held 161 hostages. The drama eventually ended when Dutch commandos successfully stormed the building.
1991 : The 'Sun' newspaper in London lost a libel suit to
a six year-old disabled boy. JOHNATHON HUNT was the youngest person to ever sue for libel.
1994 : ALEXANDER DOWNER defeated JOHN HEWSON 43 to 36 in
a vote for the leadership of the Federal Liberal Party.
